title: Censorship Of Act 1799
definition: The Censorship of Press Act, 1799 was the first legislative measure enacted by the British East India Company to impose pre-publication censorship on the press in India, primarily driven by fears of a French invasion.
importanceInUpsc: It marks the genesis of state-controlled media in colonial India, serving as the foundational precedent for subsequent restrictive acts like the Licensing Regulations of 1823 and the Vernacular Press Act of 1878.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Censorship Of Act 1799.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Evolution of British Administration in India
